title: `Expr.Data` and `Level.Data` were not conservative on extreme-depth expressions
summary: `Expr.hasLooseBVars`, `Expr.hasFVar`, `Expr.hasMVar` and friends read from the fixed-size `Expr.Data` / `Level.Data` bitfield. On overflow the kernel's `assert!`/`panic!` did not actually abort, so Lean continued with the default `0`, meaning expressions appeared to have no loose bvars / fvars / mvars when they did — a route to False. Mario Carneiro's technical write-up and proposed redesign of `Expr.Data` landed as closed PR #8554; the actual merged fix took a different approach, hardening `assert!` to abort (PRs #8559 and #8560). Affects stable versions 4.0.0 through 4.20.0 inclusive.
